svg.text: 14 — Per-layer MoE expert offload: 256 experts → 64 resident + 16 scratch + 176 host
Decisive setting: SGLANG_MOE_RESIDENT_EXPERT_FRACTION<1 (§6, [in progress]). f=0.25 on the measured run.

Only ceil(f·256)=64 experts stay resident per layer, plus a 16-slot scratch buffer; the other 176 live in pinned host RAM. Per token-wave the top-8 are gathered — resident ones read directly, spilled ones
are fetched H2D over PCIe into scratch, then the grouped GEMM runs. Wave-over-tokens keeps it coherent (§6). Upstream has no per-expert, quant-aware host spill.
htsglang — per-expert host offload, f=0.25 (§6, [in progress])
upstream sglang — no per-expert host spill
GPU — 80 expert slots resident (per layer):
64 resident (slots 0..63)
16 scratch (64..79)
Pinned host RAM — 176 spilled experts (per layer × 48 = host floor 24.4 GB):
1. router picks top-8 experts for the token-wave
2. resident hits → read on GPU directly
3. spill misses → fetch H2D over PCIe into scratch slots
4. resident + fetched → grouped GEMM → output tokens
PCIe H2D fetch
grouped GEMM
EAGER (--disable-cuda-graph): the expert set is data-dependent per wave,
so the decode path is not CUDA-graph-capturable. Graph-capture for offload: [planned].
Option A — keep all 256 experts resident in VRAM:
↑ within aggregate VRAM · ↓ beyond it
256 experts × 48 layers ≈ 65 GB vs 72 GB aggregate; per-card context +
KV must also fit, and even-TP=3 does not divide these dims (diagram 11).
Option B — --cpu-offload-gb: generic, LAYER-granular, dequantizes on
CPU, not per-expert / not quant-aware; no per-wave prefetch.
